# Zendesk CRM

Source: https://help.webexconnect.io/docs/zendesk-crm
Documentation version: 6.20.0
Retrieved: 2026-09-08T23:29:09+00:00

## Introduction

Webex Connect offers a pre-built integration node for Zendesk to make it easier for you to create a ticket in Zendesk from within an Webex Connect flow. You can also fetch the details of your existing Zendesk tickets, or add a comment to an existing ticket.

This node needs to be enabled for your account and is not available by default. Please contact your account manager in case you wish to enable it for your account.



![Screenshot of Zendesk CRM ](https://files.readme.io/b47e33f-image.png)




## Version Supported

> 📘 Webex Connect's integration is based on Zendesk API v2.

## Pre-requisites

- Client would need Zendesk account.
- Callback URLs for all your pre-built integrations, custom integration configurations, that use OAuth 2.0 authorization with ‘Auth Code’ Grant Type will be updated with Webex Connect  branded URLs. This doesn’t impact functioning of any of your existing integration configurations until the Refresh Token for that integration expires or until you decide to reauthorize. In either of these two cases, you would need to start using the new Callback URL provided on Webex Connect  UI in the third-party application you have integrated with. Another example of this is OAuth 2.0 based authentication for Gmail when using SMTP for Outbound Email channel configuration which is currently available only for Webex Connect  tenants used for Webex Contact Center Integration.  
  Please make sure your applications, firewalls, etc. do not restrict access to these new Callback URLs in case you have an internal policy/practice to add these URLs to the allow/accept/whitelist.

## Node Configuration

Drag-and-drop the node on to the visual flow builder and double-click the node to configure it.

> 📘 Please note that the latest version of the Zendesk integration node that you should use is v1.1.<Should we move this statement to the versions section>

1. Select the required **Method Name** from the drop-down list box. Examples include methods such as **Create ticket**, **Get ticket**, **Update ticket**, and **Create Chat** The following methods are supported currently:
   - [Create ticket](https://help.imiconnect.io/docs/zendesk-node-1#method-name---create-ticket)- Allows to create a new ticket with a subject, relevant description and priority of the ticket.
   - [Get ticket](https://help.imiconnect.io/docs/zendesk-node-1#method-name---get-ticket)- Allows to retrieve a ticket by unique identification number of the ticket.
   - [Update ticket](https://help.imiconnect.io/docs/zendesk-node-1#method-name---update-ticket)- Allows to modify the ticket by unique identification number of the ticket.
   - [Delete ticket](https://help.imiconnect.io/docs/zendesk-node-1#method-name---delete-ticket)- Allows to delete a specific ticket by ticket ID.  
     E.g., you can fetch all the details of the ticket like ticket number, description, category, etc. by using the **Get ticket** method



![Node Configuration](https://files.readme.io/8786505-zendesk-config.png)




2. Select add new authorization if you're using this node for the first time. You can select an existing authorization in case you've used this node in the past and have saved authorization credentials.
3. Enter the subdomain for your Zendesk account. E.g., if your Zendesk account URL is mycompanyname.zendesk.com, your subdomain is 'mycompanyname'
4. Click **Save**.
5. Once the authorization has been completed, add the request parameters for the selected method and click save. You can pass the available Input Variables or Custom Variables as request parameters.



![Screenshot of Update Ticket method configuration page.](https://files.readme.io/505fcfe-image.png)




6. You can see the data that this node generates under the Output Variables section. These [variables](https://help.webexconnect.io/docs/variable-management-in-flows) are available for use in subsequent nodes. E.g., Get ticket method returns _ticketDetails_ object as the output parameter.

7. You can see the list of possible node outcomes for this node in the below table. You can customize the node labels using the **Edit** (pencil) icon. The node exits through one of the node edges corresponding to the outcome of the node.

| <p>Node Edge</p>                                                                                                              | <p>Node Event/Outcome</p>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <p>Success (green)</p><p><strong>Note</strong>: You can see this node edge only when you complete the node configuration.</p> | <ul><li><strong>success</strong> - the flow exits through this node when the specified Zendesk method has been invoked successfully</li></ul>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| <p>Timeout (yellow/amber)</p>                                                                                                 | <ul><li><strong>onTimeout</strong> - the flow exits through this node outcome when the method could not be invoked before the timeout duration</li></ul>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| <p>Error (red)</p>                                                                                                            | <ul><li><strong>onError</strong> - the flow exits through this node outcome when there is an error in invoking the method</li><li><strong>onInvalidData</strong> - the flow exits through this node when the data is invalid</li><li><strong>onInvalidChoice</strong> - the flow exits through this node when the choice is invalid</li><li><strong>onauthorizationfail</strong> - the flow exits through this node outcome when there is an error in invoking the method</li></ul> |
